topics.topic: How admitted requests are protected and linearized against concurrent session cleanup
questions: What prevents the expiry pass from removing the session after a request passes the session check but before that request takes the session lock and uses or changes session state?
What prevents the expiry pass from ending the session and dropping its confirmation or uploaded file after a request passes the session check but before that request acquires its locks or finishes?

How is admission linearized against a cleanup pass when a request arrives before a deadline but the pass obtains the session lock and removes the session before that request obtains it, and what keeps the admitted request's session state alive until it completes?

judgement.why: This is the same admitted-request-versus-expiry-cleanup race already judged in P4, and the governing passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Outcome when expiry cleanup races an already-admitted owner request
quotes:
An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
precedent.why: Validity and idle renewal are explicitly decided at request arrival, so a request arriving before the limit remains admitted even if a sweep later obtains the lock.

topics.topic: The cleanup pass initial timing, delay and missed-run policy, and overlap behavior
questions: If a pass is delayed by locks, takes longer than 60 seconds, or the process resumes after suspension past several scheduled instants, are missed passes skipped, queued, or run immediately, and may passes overlap?

When is the first pass, and after execution delay or host/VM suspension does Registry run one immediate catch-up pass, replay every missed 60-second pass, or shift the future schedule from the delayed pass?
When is the first pass, and what happens when a pass is delayed, lasts longer than 60 seconds, or scheduled pass times are missed during suspension?

judgement.why: This repeats P6's question about the expiry pass's initial timing, delays, missed intervals, and overlap behavior on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Timing, overlap, and missed-interval behavior of the 60-second expiry pass
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: The limits themselves determine request refusal exactly, so the first tick, delayed-tick policy and overlap handling affect only internal reclamation of already inaccessible session state.

topics.topic: The cleanup pass lock scope and permitted concurrent session-map changes
questions: Does one pass hold the import lock while it visits all sessions, acquire and release each session lock in turn, or acquire all session locks together; and may requests create or remove sessions while the pass enumerates them?

Does one pass hold the import lock for the entire traversal, acquiring and releasing session locks one at a time, or reacquire the import lock separately for each session; and may it hold more than one session lock at once?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P15 about import-lock and session-lock scope during expiry traversal, with no relevant textual change.

precedent.topic: Import-lock and session-lock scope during an expiry pass
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: Holding the import lock for the whole visit or per session, and snapshotting or dynamically enumerating sessions, changes only internal waiting and reclamation because validity is decided from the fixed limits at request arrival.

topics.topic: Whether host suspension ends all sessions or merely advances their expiration clocks
questions: Does any suspension end every session, or does suspension merely count toward the 8-hour, 30-minute, 15-minute and 10-minute limits so that a short suspension may leave a session valid?
Does every suspension end every owner session on resume, or does suspension merely advance the duration clocks so that only sessions whose 8-hour or 30-minute deadline passed expire?

judgement.why: This repeats P20's question whether suspension itself ends sessions or merely consumes their duration limits, on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Owner-session behavior during host or VM suspension
quotes:
Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10
   minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock,
   which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time
   the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a
   suspension; instants Registry records
   and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
precedent.why: Suspended time consumes the ordinary duration limits; suspension is not stated as an independent event that ends every session.

topics.topic: Whether session expiry immediately removes the session and temporary state or only invalidates it until cleanup
questions: Does reaching a limit end and remove the session immediately, or only make it invalid until a later pass removes it and drops its confirmation and uploaded file?
At a time limit, does the session and its temporary state end immediately, or does it merely become invalid until the next cleanup pass formally ends it and drops that state?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P19 about exact expiry invalidation versus deferred removal of the session and temporary state.

precedent.topic: Exact expiry time versus deferred session and resource cleanup
quotes:
The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable).

A session that has reached a
   limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check. Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.
precedent.why: The session becomes invalid exactly at its limit, while removal of its stored confirmation, upload and runtime record occurs during the periodic pass.

topics.topic: How concurrent request arrivals extend the idle deadline before last_request is updated
questions: How can a later request validate against an earlier concurrent arrival that should have restarted the idle period but has not yet acquired the session lock or updated `last_request`?

topics.topic: The exact request-arrival boundary used for idle-deadline calculations
questions: At what exact processing boundary is a request considered to have arrived, and is that captured before any queueing or lock wait?
